984b9f951f.q: Why did FourEyes choose to build open infrastructure for dealerships instead of closed proprietary software?
984b9f951f.a: David Steinberg explained that automotive diverged from the rest of the economy around 2016-2017 by closing off data through silos and walled gardens, while other industries embraced open ecosystems. He argues this is backwards and hurts dealers. FourEyes believes the right approach is providing open access and connectivity so dealers can build custom solutions with AI, rather than forcing them into all-in-one packaged software that underperforms, comparing it to the failure of all-in-one printers.

7e746b2913.q: How does incomplete data versus complete data affect AI-driven marketing analysis and reporting accuracy?
7e746b2913.a: Brian Pasch emphasized that incomplete data looks exactly like complete data, creating a critical problem. When tools on websites don't send conversion events into Google Analytics 4 (GA4), marketing analysis produces broken and inaccurate reports. The KPI MCP server solves this by flagging whether data is complete or incomplete, allowing builders to trust reports only for stores with complete data before running marketing analysis.

4312667146.q: How does FourEyes structure the data collection and activation process for dealers embracing AI?
4312667146.a: FourEyes follows four stages: collect all data (phone calls, inventory, website, DMS, CRM), connect it via custom connectors, visualize it, and activate it. They put data into Snowflake or the customer's preferred data warehouse and wrap an API layer around it allowing functionality like sending messages, monitoring consent, recording campaigns, and building automations. This API access enables Claude to build campaigns, schedule them, monitor results, and store data so dealers can access it in unlimited ways.
